correctness.rationale: The exact one-circle minimax is cos(half maximal cyclic gap) even when negative. Orthogonal decomposability reduces the 4D minimax to one signed scalar minimax and yields all three branches including empty-factor limits. Consecutive deletion blocks uniquely maximize cyclic gaps, so each polygon first obtains a negative minimum after floor(n/2) deletions; both factors must be negative (except the strictly more expensive empty-factor case), proving floor(p/2)+floor(q/2), exactly pq patterns and unique deepest directions. The square–pentagon sign census, angular complement and critical constants follow from these identities. Standard-library and independently optimized convex-hull checks passed on actual packaged files; finite checks corroborate the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The natural covering robustness of two-plane spherical site constructions is completely characterized for every deletion subset in infinitely many p,q configurations. It identifies the precise first erasure budget that drives global covering past a hemisphere, counts exactly all critical configurations, and supplies unique deepest points and sharp angular values. In the proven maximal-volume nine-site configuration there is an unexpectedly flat 90-degree plateau and precisely twenty four-site catastrophic patterns. The result is a motivated full classification, not an arbitrary finite enumeration; it does not assert optimality among other codes.
